paragraphs: Fostering for children in care in Northampton is run by Northamptonshire Children's Trust, which recruits, trains and supports foster carers for both West Northamptonshire Council and North Northamptonshire Council. The independent services shown above also cover the town.

Ofsted inspected the trust's fostering service in January 2024 and judged it good, a rise from inadequate in just twelve months; inspectors noted significant improvements in how foster carers are supported and supervised. Announcing the result, the trust's chief executive spoke of a huge shortage of foster carers and asked anyone who had been thinking about fostering to get in touch.

Several of the trust's recruitment events have been held in Northampton. Over the winter of 2024 to 2025 the trust held an open evening at Nene Retail Park and drop-in sessions at the Savoy Theatre, and its fostering service manager set out the basics: you must be over 21, have a spare room and live permanently in the UK, and there is no upper age limit, with carers in their late seventies. During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026, under the national theme This Is Fostering, the trust and both councils held an information evening at the Old Savoy Theatre where people could talk to experienced carers and staff, and launched a Fostering Friendly Pledge asking local businesses to back foster carers with discounts, wellbeing support or flexible services.

Fostering with the trust means caring for Northamptonshire's own children, with training and a social worker from the trust. An independent agency approves, trains and supports you itself and takes children referred by councils and trusts, this one among them. The trust does not publish a current pay scale that we can link to, so ask it and each agency for their fees and allowances and compare them. Speak to the trust and to two or three of the services above before you choose. Nearby, see our pages for Northamptonshire, Milton Keynes, Bedfordshire and Leicestershire.
